To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the study of seabirds can help to improve marine conservation and management.
the seabirds’ eye view is a promising approach for marine conservation and that it can be used to improve the management of common-pool marine resource in both protected and unprotected areas.

1) seabirds’ movements can be used as a proxy for ecosystem health; 2) seabirds are a useful tool for marine spatial planning; 3) seabirds can be used as indicators of marine protected areas’ effectiveness and as a tool for marine spatial management; and 4) seabirds have the potential to help in bridging the gap between science and management, and to foster the involvement of stakeholders in marine conservation and management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods and tools for marine conservation and management.

the development of a new path to marine conservation, based on the use of top-predators and the development of a more integrated approach to marine conservation, which acknowledges the interdependencies within and across marine ecosystems.
the following questions: How can we use seabirds to better understand marine ecosystems?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
seabirds are a powerful tool for marine conservation, which can help to meet the challenge of managing common-pooled marine resources.

the use of seabirds as sentinels of the marine environment is a useful tool to help understand and monitor the marine environment, to improve the management of the marine environment, and to increase the awareness of stakeholders towards the marine environment.
seabirds are a useful tool for marine conservation, but that the value of their use depends upon the research question, the available data, and the management context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
seabirds are good indicators of the health of the oceans, they help us understand the dynamics of marine ecosystems and they provide a way for people to connect to marine conservation.
seabirds are a good indicator for marine ecosystems, but also that seabirds can be used as indicators of human activities and as tools for engaging stakeholders and for promoting conservation.

seabirds are a good proxy for the marine environment and that seabird-based research can help to identify and understand marine ecosystem services, and their interactions with human activities, in order to better inform marine conservation and management.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to achieve the goals of marine management, we need to develop a more comprehensive understanding of how different marine ecosystems are connected and how this affects the management of the resources they provide.

, in order to meet the challenges of the Anthropocene, we need to move from a single-species to a multi-species approach to conservation and to management, and that this should include a better integration of the social and ecological sciences, and a more explicit consideration of the role of stakeholders in marine ecosystems.
seabirds are excellent tools for marine conservation, as their presence and absence in the marine ecosystem is linked with a number of key issues.
